html:
The Khojaly massacre was the killing of Azerbaijani civilians fleeing the town of Khojaly in Nagorno Karabakh on 26 February 1992, after Armenian forces, with help from a Russian regiment, captured it.

Khojaly, near Stepanakert, held the region's only airport. Its residents tried to escape through the snow toward Azerbaijani lines and were fired on. The Azerbaijani parliament counted 613 dead, including many women and children; Human Rights Watch called it the largest massacre of the conflict. The killing brought down the Azerbaijani president Ayaz Mutallibov. It is remembered every year in Azerbaijan and became a key grievance of the Karabakh war, recalled in the war of 2020.
sum: The Khojaly massacre was the killing of Azerbaijani civilians fleeing the town of Khojaly in Nagorno Karabakh on 26 February 1992, after Armenian forces, with help from a Russian regiment, captured it.
